title: How to Build a Realistic IA Marking Schedule
summary: Learn how to build a realistic IA marking schedule that protects standardisation, moderation and admin time while balancing competing IB deadlines.
body_markdown:
An effective **IA marking schedule** works backwards from the school’s handover dates, then reserves separate time for first marking, standardisation, review, administration and unexpected delays. It should not assume that every available planning period can become a productive marking session.


For IB Diploma Programme teachers, the challenge is arranging enough focused time while reports, mock examinations and coursework deadlines compete for attention. The framework below provides a practical method for planning grading time across a term without compromising consistency.


### Start with the deadlines that cannot move


Begin with the calendar issued by your DP coordinator. School deadlines normally precede IB submission requirements because teachers and coordinators need time to mark work, standardise decisions, enter marks, identify moderation samples and prepare files.


Distinguish four dates for every component:


Date What it controls


Student final submission When complete, authenticable work reaches the teacher


Marking completion When criterion marks and comments must be finished


Internal standardisation When colleagues align their application of the criteria


Coordinator handover When marks and files are ready for checking or upload


These dates are school-specific. Use the coordinator’s confirmed calendar rather than an old handbook, another school’s policy or an online discussion.


IB moderation checks how accurately and consistently teachers apply assessment criteria. The IB’s[assessment principles and practices](https://ibo.org/contentassets/1cdf850e366447e99b5a862aab622883/assessment-principles-and-practices-2018-en.pdf) explains how moderation supports a common global standard. Standardisation and checking are therefore essential scheduled stages, not optional additions.
